title: Finalize install broker setup safe operations and risk documentation
description:
Write the final operator-facing documentation for requirements, safety/risk controls, test plan, dashboard, and Alpaca broker setup. All of it must match the implemented product and the t.1 deployment artifacts.

Before editing, inspect:
- deploy/systemd/mike-trade-engine.service and deploy/systemd/mike-trade-dashboard.service (from t.1)
- mike_trade/controls/service_manager.py and the other mike_trade/controls/ modules (operator commands, live confirmation)
- Makefile and the CLI entrypoint (complete operator command surface)
- mike_trade/brokers/ (Alpaca adapter, capability matrix, paper/live endpoint isolation, IEX feed provenance)
- mike_trade/risk/, mike_trade/protection/, mike_trade/reconciliation/ (budgets, lockouts, cooldown, stops, drift)
- mike_trade/dashboard/ and the frontend build configuration
- existing docs/ files

Implementation requirements:
1. docs/REQUIREMENTS.md: the self-contained product contract as implemented. Cover scope (1-10 U.S. equities, long-only, one entry and one full exit per cycle, no averaging/pyramiding/planned partials), the four modes (BACKTEST, SHADOW, PAPER, LIVE) and their isolation, Decimal/UTC conventions, persistence (SQLite WAL, migrations, append-only audit, no raw tick archive), strategies (vwap_bounce/vwap_breakdown/vwap_reference semantics), and the explicit out-of-scope list.
2. docs/SAFETY_AND_RISK.md: per-symbol and total budgets, buying-power checks, planned-loss sizing, max open positions, daily loss guard, daily entry-cycle cap, symbol and buy-strategy loss lockouts, post-sale cooldown, minimum hold (ordinary exits only), regular-hours/entry cutoff/early close, optional EOD close disabled by default, protective stop coverage rules (fixed/native trailing/stepped trailing, post-fill start, remaining-quantity coverage, never downward, offline survival limits, no oversell), fail-closed conditions, the distinction between stop/pause/entry kill switch/close/close-all/flatten, shutdown semantics, startup reconciliation, UNMANAGED external positions, live confirmation requirements, credential storage (root-owned 0600 env files, per-mode separation), state directory permissions, backup/restore and integrity-check procedures, and the incident runbook.
3. docs/TEST_PLAN.md: test layers (unit, integration, offline end-to-end, credential-gated paper), how to run targeted tests, the mapping of the required acceptance scenarios to test files (tests/end_to_end/test_full_product_cycle.py, tests/end_to_end/test_recovery_offline.py, tests/end_to_end/test_protective_live_guards.py, tests/paper_broker/test_alpaca_paper_cycle.py), paper gating env vars and the approval opt-in, a statement that no automated live orders are ever run, and the policy of one deliberate final comprehensive pass only with operator authorization.
4. docs/DASHBOARD.md: the separate FastAPI read-only process serving the compiled React/TypeScript/Vite bundle, build and deploy steps (no Vite dev server in production), systemd unit usage, independence from the engine, OFFLINE determination from heartbeat age, stale value marking, account/scenario switching without mixed balances, the panels shown, and the statement that it never places orders or mutates configuration.
5. docs/ALPACA.md: account and API key setup for paper and live, endpoint isolation, env file layout and permissions, Basic IEX feed limitations and provenance (not consolidated SIP), trade_updates stream, the order/protection capability matrix with each combination marked supported/verified-in-paper/blocked, fractional restrictions (fail closed until demonstrated in paper), the paper verification procedure, a warning that paper fills do not prove live performance, and live enablement prerequisites.
6. Every Make/CLI command referenced must exist in the Makefile/CLI. Do not document nonexistent commands. Mark externally gated items (paper verification) as pending until performed by the operator.
acceptance_criteria: All five files (docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, docs/SAFETY_AND_RISK.md, docs/TEST_PLAN.md, docs/DASHBOARD.md, docs/ALPACA.md) exist and contain substantive operator-usable content, not placeholders.
docs/SAFETY_AND_RISK.md explicitly distinguishes stop, pause, entry kill switch, close, close-all, and flatten, and states that shutdown does not liquidate positions or cancel valid protective stops.
docs/SAFETY_AND_RISK.md documents credential env file location/ownership/0600 permissions, per-mode separation, state directory permissions, backup/restore, and integrity-check steps.

docs/ALPACA.md states that Basic IEX is not consolidated SIP data, documents paper/live endpoint isolation, and contains a capability matrix that marks unsupported or unverified fractional/protective combinations as blocked.

docs/TEST_PLAN.md maps the required final acceptance scenarios to specific test files and states that the paper suite requires credentials plus explicit approval and that no automated live orders are run.
docs/DASHBOARD.md states that the dashboard is a separate read-only process serving a compiled build, determines OFFLINE from heartbeat age, and never places orders or mutates configuration.
Every Make target or CLI command named in these documents exists in the repository's Makefile or CLI.
No document contains real credentials or claims that paper or live verification has passed when it has not been performed.
forbidden_changes: change PLAN_SKELETON.json or any planning artifacts under .abracapocus/
document commands, capabilities, or verification results that do not exist
include real credentials, account numbers, or tokens
claim profitability or live performance from paper or shadow results
